title: Level 0: Cloud Observability 1000-Foot View
subtitle: Orientation-only map for safe positioning and shared observability vocabulary

nodes.label: Cloud Observability
nodes.definition: A way to understand system behavior by connecting telemetry signals.
nodes.whyItMatters: It provides one connected view of system health and risk.
nodes.safeSentence: I see observability as the modern way to connect metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerts, and runbooks into operational understanding.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not reduce observability to only dashboards.

nodes.label: Telemetry
nodes.definition: Data emitted by systems so people and tools can understand behavior.
nodes.whyItMatters: Telemetry is the evidence used for monitoring, troubleshooting, and planning.
nodes.safeSentence: Telemetry is the raw evidence used for monitoring, troubleshooting, capacity, and reporting.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat telemetry as useful unless it is organized and interpreted.

note.summary: Source evidence for all observability work.

nodes.label: Metrics
nodes.definition: Numbers measured over time, such as CPU, memory, latency, and errors.
nodes.whyItMatters: Metrics reveal trend and threshold changes quickly.
nodes.safeSentence: Metrics help me see trends, thresholds, headroom, and capacity risk.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not look at one metric alone without context.

note.summary: Time-series indicators for health and risk.

nodes.label: Logs
nodes.definition: Text records that describe events, errors, warnings, and system activity.
nodes.whyItMatters: Logs provide context around failures and anomalies.
nodes.safeSentence: Logs help explain what happened around an event or failure.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not confuse logs with metrics.

nodes.label: Traces
nodes.definition: A request path across services showing timing and failure points.
nodes.whyItMatters: Traces reveal where delay or failure occurred across dependencies.
nodes.safeSentence: Traces help connect user or service requests to where time or failure occurred.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not claim deep tracing ownership before hands-on practice.

nodes.label: APM
nodes.definition: Application Performance Monitoring focuses on application health, transactions, latency, errors, and dependencies.
nodes.whyItMatters: APM helps teams monitor service behavior and user impact.
nodes.safeSentence: My older APM background helps me understand the purpose of modern observability.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not say APM and observability are identical.

nodes.label: Dashboards
nodes.definition: Visual views that summarize system behavior for humans.
nodes.whyItMatters: Dashboards make telemetry easier to consume for operations and leadership.
nodes.safeSentence: Dashboards turn telemetry into something operators and leaders can use.
nodes.commonTrap: A dashboard without action or context is just decoration.

note.summary: Visual operating surface for key signals.

nodes.label: Alerts
nodes.definition: Rules or signals that notify people when attention is needed.
nodes.whyItMatters: Alerts trigger timely response to real risk.
nodes.safeSentence: Good alerts should point to risk or action, not just noise.

nodes.label: Runbooks
nodes.definition: Step-by-step guidance for what to check and do during an issue.
nodes.whyItMatters: Runbooks improve consistency and speed during incidents.
nodes.safeSentence: Runbooks turn monitoring into repeatable operational response.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not create alerts without response guidance.

nodes.label: Capacity Monitoring
nodes.definition: Watching resource usage and headroom to avoid shortages or waste.
nodes.whyItMatters: Capacity awareness reduces outage and cost risk.
nodes.safeSentence: Capacity monitoring is one of my strongest bridges into cloud observability.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not talk only about CPU; capacity includes memory, disk, network, throughput, and demand patterns.

nodes.label: Capacity Forecasting
nodes.definition: Using history and trends to estimate future resource risk.
nodes.whyItMatters: Forecasting supports proactive scaling and planning.
nodes.safeSentence: Forecasting turns telemetry into planning information.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not oversell forecasting as perfect prediction.

nodes.label: Business Reporting
nodes.definition: Turning technical signals into risk, trend, cost, and planning summaries.
nodes.whyItMatters: Leaders need clear risk framing for decisions.
nodes.safeSentence: My strength is translating telemetry into decisions leaders can act on.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not bury leaders in raw metrics.

nodes.label: Sean Skill Bridge
nodes.definition: The path from enterprise APM and capacity work to cloud observability.
nodes.whyItMatters: It provides honest positioning while building modern depth.
nodes.safeSentence: My foundation is real monitoring and capacity experience; I am updating the tooling layer.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not pretend every new tool is already deep production experience.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry
nodes.definition: A modern standard for collecting and moving telemetry.
nodes.whyItMatters: It enables vendor-neutral telemetry collection patterns.
nodes.safeSentence: I understand OpenTelemetry as a vendor-neutral telemetry collection pattern that I am building practical experience with.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not claim production OTel platform ownership yet.

nodes.label: Prometheus / Grafana / CloudWatch / Vendors
nodes.definition: Common tools used for metrics, dashboards, cloud monitoring, and APM.
nodes.whyItMatters: Tool-fit awareness supports better design and interview communication.
nodes.safeSentence: At Level 0, I can explain where the tools fit before claiming deep hands-on ownership.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not confuse knowing the landscape with owning every platform.
